Secure Model Validation

Source: R/secure_model_validation.R
secure_model_validation.Rd

Retrieves a clinical prediction model specification from a developer's private GitHub repository and computes predictions locally on the evaluator's dataset, without transmitting patient data.

Usage

secure_model_validation(
  repo_owner,
  repo_name,
  model_id,
  github_token,
  validation_data,
  outcome,
  by = NULL
)

Arguments

repo_owner

Character. GitHub username or organisation owning the model repository.

repo_name

Character. Name of the GitHub repository containing the model specification.

model_id

Character. Unique identifier for the model (must match the folder name under models/ in the repository).

github_token

Character. Fine-grained GitHub personal access token with read-only access to the repository. Provided by the model developer.

validation_data

Data frame. The evaluator's local dataset, which must contain all predictor variables required by the model.

outcome

Character. Name of the outcome variable in validation_data.

by

Character or NULL. Optional name of a grouping variable in validation_data for subgroup analysis (e.g. "study"). Must have at least two non-missing categories, each meeting the minimum observation requirement.

Value

A named list of class evaluatr_result containing:

shuffled_outcome_predictions

Matrix of shuffled outcome-prediction pairs (and subgroup column if by is specified).

shuffled_outcomes

Numeric vector of shuffled outcomes.

shuffled_predictions

Numeric vector of shuffled predicted probabilities (binary models only).

shuffled_by

Vector of shuffled subgroup values (only present when by is specified).

prediction_matrix

Matrix of shuffled predicted probabilities (multinomial models: one column per outcome category).

model_info

List of model metadata including model_id, model_name, model_type, version, required_variables, n_predictions, and validation_timestamp.

Details

A minimum dataset size is enforced (per subgroup when by is used). Predictions are shuffled before being returned so that they cannot be matched back to individual patient records, preventing reverse-engineering of model coefficients and ensuring the system cannot be used to make predictions for individual patients in clinical practice.

Patient data is never transmitted outside your R session. The validation event is logged by the evaluatr registry.

To use this function you need four items from the model developer: their GitHub username, repository name, model ID, and a time-limited access token. See the evaluator guide vignette (vignette("evaluator-guide", package = "evaluatr")) for a step-by-step walkthrough. Use list_registered_models() to browse publicly registered models and find developer contact details.

See also

eval_performance() for computing performance metrics from the returned object. list_registered_models() to browse publicly registered models.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Load the DVT example dataset included with the package
dvt_path <- system.file("extdata", "dvt_example.csv", package = "evaluatr")
dvt_data <- read.csv(dvt_path)

# Use only studies 6-7 as the external validation set
dvt_val <- dvt_data[dvt_data$study %in% c(6, 7), ]

# Run secure validation against the public evaluatr demo model. For your
# own models, replace these values with those supplied by the developer.
result <- secure_model_validation(
  repo_owner      = "JoieEnsor",
  repo_name       = "evaluatr-demo-models",
  model_id        = "dvt_logistic_v1",
  github_token    = "evaluatr-demo",
  validation_data = dvt_val,
  outcome         = "dvt"
)

# Compute performance metrics
perf <- eval_performance(result)
perf$metrics

# Subgroup analysis by study
result_by_study <- secure_model_validation(
  repo_owner      = "JoieEnsor",
  repo_name       = "evaluatr-demo-models",
  model_id        = "dvt_logistic_v1",
  github_token    = "evaluatr-demo",
  validation_data = dvt_val,
  outcome         = "dvt",
  by              = "study"
)

perf_by_study <- eval_performance(
  result_by_study,
  by = result_by_study$shuffled_by
)
perf_by_study$metrics
} # }
